learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with the fundamentals of chemical reactions useful for the identification of material properties and for the design of reactors and bioreactors.
Understand the mechanisms underlying chemical reactions.
Perform experimental determination of kinetic parameters.
Understand thermal effects in materials formation.
Evaluate and optimize different reactor configurations.
Predict the behavior of materials on the basis of chemical structure.
Set up and solve the fundamental equations describing different configurations of homogeneous and heterogeneous chemical reactors.
Analyze experimental data and interpret them for the purpose of developing homogeneous and heterogeneous kinetic models.
Optimize reactor configuration, including consideration of thermal effects.
Acquire sensitivity in carrying out activities to analyze experimental data and interpret them.
Acquire sensitivity in understanding the effect of various phenomena present in chemical reactors.
Acquire sensitivity in evaluating optimal operating conditions.

syllabus_topics: THE STRUCTURE OF MATTER: The structure of atoms.
Valence bond theory, hybridization, molecular orbital theory.
The metallic bond and band theory, conductors, semiconductors and insulators.
THE CHEMICAL THERMODYNAMICS: the first principle of thermodynamics and thermochemistry.
The second principle of thermodynamics and the spontaneity of chemical/biochemical reactions.
THE CHEMICAL EQUILIBRATION: homogeneous equilibria in the gas phase.
THE CHEMICAL KINETICS: the rate of a chemical reaction.
Reaction orders, effects of temperature on rate.
Complex and enzymatic reactions, mechanisms of reactions.
CRYSTALLINE AND AMORPHIC STRUCTURE OF MATERIALS: Bravais lattices, main metal structures, comparison of CFC, EC, CCC structures.
Planar volume density, polymorphism and allotropy.
THERMICALLY ACTIVATED PROCESSES: solidification of metals, solid metal solutions.
POLYMERIC MATERIALS: Polymerization reactions, industrial processes for polymerization.
Cross flow stationary reactor, piston flow stationary reactor.
Classroom exercises on all topics covered.
teaching_methods: Lectures (participatory lecture with direct student intervention)

assessment_methods.method: Written test (end of second semester, for those who failed/did not take the first test, or average with first test)

assessment_rules: Students have the opportunity to pass the first part of the course (first semester) through an ad hoc written test. The result of this test, expressed in thirtieths, will be averaged with the result of the test at the end of the second semester. For those who fail or do not take the first test, they will be allowed to take a single written test at the end of the course on all topics covered in both semesters. The final grade is based on an oral exam after knowledge verification tests.
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Medica classe L-9 R Ingegneria industriale
